title: Evaluation of consumer health information about monkeypox on X (formerly Twitter)
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study (INSTRUCTIONS section 1 exclusion, section 3 rule). The 279 Mpox tweets are scored on the Global Quality Scale (usefulness/completeness for patients) and the modified DISCERN reliability instrument (aims clear, sources cited, balance, further sources, uncertainty). Neither instrument judges a post true or false: a wholly accurate tweet scores 1 on the GQS if it is thin, and 0 on DISCERN items if it cites no sources. The Methods say accuracy was checked against WHO and CDC fact sheets, but no accuracy share is reported anywhere in the Results, the Tables or the Abstract, so there is no share of posts classified false, misleading or inaccurate to extract.
missed_or_uncertain: JUDGEMENT CALL for the adjudicator. Section 1 lists QUALITY-ONLY studies as an exclusion ground while section 3 says a quality-scored value becomes a row with construct=QUALITY that is 'kept, excluded from prevalence'; section 5 says the estimates list must be empty when the screen is EXCLUDE. I followed the screen rule and wrote no rows, but every candidate value is recorded here verbatim so a QUALITY row can be created without re-reading the paper. Sample: 279 English-language tweets with at least five retweets, retrieved 27 November 2024 from five hashtags (#Mpox, #Monkeypox, #Mpoxvaccine, #MpoxOutbreak, #MonkeypoxVaccine), posted between 1 January 2021 and 31 October 2024; two independent trained reviewers, Cohen's kappa = 0.82; country not stated (English-language X, effectively global). GQS distribution (Table 3, n=279): 'Using the GQS, 86 posts (30.8%) were rated as having very low quality, 77 posts (27.6%) received a medium quality rating, and only 33 posts (11.8%) were rated as very high quality' - full table: very low 86 (30.8%), low 49 (17.6%), medium 77 (27.6%), high 34 (12.2%), very high 33 (11.8%). DISCERN distribution (Table 4, n=279): 'Using the DISCERN score, 80 posts (28.7%) were rated as having very low reliability, and 46 posts (16.5%) as low reliability' - full table: very low 80 (28.7%), low 46 (16.5%), medium 89 (31.8%), high 30 (10.8%), very high 34 (12.2%). The Abstract's 'Almost half of the posts (45.2%) had very low to low reliability' is the authors' own sum of the two lowest DISCERN bands and is stated verbatim. Also not extracted, because they are not misinformation shares: poster type (individuals 45.5%, news outlets 23.7%, non-health professionals 69.2% combined, health professionals 17.6%, health organizations 13.3%), engagement bands, hashtag shares, post-format shares, the topic composition of posts (prevalence 32.3%, description 26.5%, etc.), and the mean GQS values by poster type (individuals 2.35 +/- 1.28 to health professionals 2.82 +/- 1.33, p=0.154), which are scale means with no share attached. The 60% of Mpox posts made by individuals and the DISCERN mean of 39.56/80 for TikTok are figures the paper cites from Ortiz-Martinez et al. 2022 and Shi et al. 2023, not its own data.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of X posts retrieved on a single day (27 November 2024) through five hashtags using two purpose-built gender-neutral accounts with fixed interest settings to limit algorithmic personalisation; inclusion restricted to English-language posts with at least five retweets that provided information about Mpox, posted 1 January 2021 - 31 October 2024, yielding 279 tweets. Each of the reviewers was assigned one calendar year and coded independently after training; agreement Cohen's kappa = 0.82. Instruments: modified DISCERN (five yes/no items) and the five-point Global Quality Scale. Authors note the hashtag set and the short window may make the sample unrepresentative.
